course_info.faculty: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences

catalog_course_description: Theories and approaches to understanding psychopathology and treatment to, and prevention of abnormal behavior. Emphasis is on current theory, research, issues in, and the role of clinical psychology in contemporary society.
course_learning_outcomes: Students will gain knowledge of the predominant features of specific psychological disorders, including characteristics of behavior, etiology, prevalence, and prognosis.
Students will understand how our current knowledge of abnormal behavior can be applied to improve the lives of suffering individuals
course_objective: Abnormal Psychology course is an introductory survey for abnormality and psychopathology. We will review the symptoms and characteristics of various psychological disorders, discuss current research and controversies in the field, and briefly focus on the treatments of mental health problems. Throughout the course, we will look at major research issues as they relate to both the causal factors of each disorder and the efficacy of current treatments and interventions.

resources: There will be a reading packet for this course that consist of empirical papers, case materials, and chapters. Please follow the SUCourse for the uploaded readings.
